farraa:1-5.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿وَلَمْ يَجْعَل لَّهُ عِوَجَا قَيِّماً﴾ (and has not made in it any crookedness — straight): the meaning is: praise be to Allah who sent down the Book to His servant straight (قَيِّما), and has not made in it any crookedness. It is also said of القيّم: a guardian over the (other) scriptures, i.e. it confirms them.
His saying ﴿لِّيُنْذِرَ بَأْساً شَدِيداً﴾ (to warn of a severe punishment): along with "the punishment" there are suppressed nouns on which the verb falls before it falls on "the punishment". Similar is (the verse) in Āl ʿImrān: ﴿إنَّما ذَلِكُمُ الشَّيطَان يُخَوِّف أَوْلِيَاءَهُ﴾ (that is only Satan who frightens [you] of his allies); its meaning is: he frightens you of his allies.
His saying: ﴿مَّا لَهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ وَلاَ لآبَائِهِمْ﴾ (they have no knowledge of it, nor did their fathers): its meaning is: nor their forebears — their fathers and their fathers' fathers; [and not] meaning only the fathers who are their immediate begetters.
His saying: ﴿كَبُرَتْ كَلِمَةً تَخْرُجُ مِنْ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ﴾ (grave is the word that comes out of their mouths): the companions of ʿAbdallāh made it (كلمة) accusative, and al-Ḥasan and some of the people of Medina made it nominative. Whoever makes it accusative suppresses (a subject) in (كبرت): "that word is grave as a word". Whoever makes it nominative suppresses nothing; just as you say: "your statement is enormous, and your speech is grave".

farraa:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿وَهَيِّىءْ﴾ (and prepare): the hamza was written with alif — (وهَيَّأْ) — according to its spelling. The hamza is mostly written according to what precedes it: if what precedes it has fatḥa, it is written with alif; if ḍamma, it is written with wāw; and if kasra, it is written with yāʾ. Sometimes the Arabs wrote it with alif in every case, because its origin is alif. They said: we see that when it is initial it is written with alif whether it has fatḥa, kasra or ḍamma; as in your saying أُمِروا, أَمَرت, and ﴿وقد جئتَ شيئاً إمْرا﴾ (you have done a grievous thing); so they followed this approach. He said: I saw it in the codex of ʿAbdallāh (شيْأً), with alif in its nominative and genitive (forms), and I saw يستهزءون written يستهزأون with alif; and that is the analogical form. The first (way) is more common in the written copies.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿فَضَرَبْنَا عَلَىٰ آذَانِهِمْ﴾ (so We cast [a cover] over their ears): with sleep.
His saying: ﴿سِنِينَ عَدَداً﴾ (for a number of years): العَدَد here is in the sense of "counted" (معدودة), and Allah knows best. When what precedes العدد is a named number, like the hundred, the thousand, the ten and the five, there are two aspects for العدد. One is that you make it accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), so you say: لك عندى عشرة عَدَداً (I owe you ten, by count); you derive "count" from "ten", because "ten" contains the meaning "they were counted", as though you said: they were reckoned and counted, by count (عَدَداً and عَدّا). And if you wish you make العدد nominative, meaning: you have ten counted (ones). So العدد here, with "years", is like His saying, Blessed and Exalted, in (Sūrat) Yūsuf: ﴿وَشَرَوْهُ بِثَمَنٍ بَخْسٍ دَرَاهِمَ مَعْدُودَةٍ﴾ (and they sold him for a paltry price, a few counted dirhams), because the dirhams are not named by a number. Likewise whatever is measured by volume or weight: you produce it (when it comes) after its names in the two ways. So you say: لك عندى عشرة أرطال وَزناً and وَزنٌ (I owe you ten raṭls by weight), and كيلاً and كيلٌ (by measure), on that basis.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿لِنَعْلَمَ أَيُّ الحِزْبَيْنِ أَحْصَىٰ﴾ (that We might make evident which of the two parties was more precise in reckoning): you make أىّ nominative by أحصى (i.e. as mubtadaʾ (subject) with أحصى as its khabar (predicate)), because "knowing" does not fall upon أىّ; it is only: "that you may know by looking and asking". It is like your saying: "go and find out for me which of them stood", for do you not see that you only make the knowing fall on the one from whom you seek information. What makes that clear is that you say: سَلْ عبدَالله أَيُّهم قامَ (ask ʿAbdallāh which of them stood); if you dropped ʿAbdallāh, you would still be intending him, or someone like him among those who give information.
His saying: ﴿أَيُّ الحِزْبَيْنِ﴾ (which of the two parties): it is said that two groups of Muslims in the time of the companions of the cave differed about their number. It is also said: the disbelievers and the Muslims differed. As for (أَحْصَىٰ), it is said: more correct, i.e. which of them spoke correctly.
His saying: ﴿أَمَداً﴾ (in period): أمدا may be accusative in two ways. If you wish, you make it derive from ﴿أَحْصَىٰ﴾ as a specifying explanation (tamyīz (specification)), as you say: "which of the two parties is more correct in speech"; and if you wish, you make the "staying" fall on it: for their staying a period.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِذِ ٱعْتَزَلْتُمُوهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ﴾ (and since you have withdrawn from them and what they worship) means the companions of the cave. He said: since you have withdrawn from all the gods they worship except Allah. (ما) is in the position of the accusative. That is because they used to associate partners with Allah, so He said: you have withdrawn from the idols, but you have not withdrawn from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, nor from His worship.
His saying: ﴿فَأْوُوا إِلَى ٱلْكَهْفِ﴾ (then take refuge in the cave) is the answer to إذْ, as you say: "since you have done what you did, then repent".
His saying: ﴿مِّنْ أَمْرِكُمْ مِّرْفَقاً﴾ (some ease in your affair): al-Aʿmash and al-Ḥasan gave the mīm kasra, and the people of Medina and ʿĀṣim gave it fatḥa. It seems that those who gave the mīm fatḥa and the fāʾ kasra wished to distinguish between المَرْفِق "of an affair" and المِرْفَق "of a person" (the elbow). Most of the Arabs give the mīm kasra both for the affair and for the person. The Arabs also give the mīm fatḥa in مرفق of a person. They are two dialect forms in both.

farraa:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿تَّزَاوَرُ﴾ (it inclines away): it has also been read ﴿تزَّاوَرُ﴾, meaning (تَتَزاور), the tāʾ being assimilated into the zāy. Some read (تَزْوَرّ) and some (تَزْوَارّ), like تَحْمرّ and تَحْمارّ. The inclining away (الازورار) here is that it (the sun) would rise upon their cave on the right side and not enter upon them, and (likewise) on the left side. The Arabs say: قرضته ذات اليمين (I passed it on the right) and حَذَوته (I was alongside it), and likewise ذات الشمال (on the left), قُبُلا (in front) and دُبُرا (behind) — all of that meaning: I was alongside it on every side.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿ذِرَاعَيْهِ بِٱلوَصِيدِ﴾ (its forelegs at the threshold): الوَصِيد is the courtyard (al-fināʾ). الوصيد and الأَصيد are two dialect forms, like الإكَاف and الوِكَاف (pack-saddle), and like أَرَّخْت الكتاب and وَرَّخته (I dated the letter), وكَّدت الأمر and أكَّدته (I confirmed the matter), and وضعْتُه يَتْنا, أَتْنا and وَتْنَا, meaning the child (born feet first). As for the Arabs' saying واخيت, وامرت, واتيت and واسيت, these are built on المواخاة, المواسَاة, المواتاة and الموامرة, and their origin is with hamza; just as it is said: هو سْوَل منك, whose origin is with hamza, and it was changed into wāw and built on السوَال.
His saying: ﴿فِي فَجْوَةٍ مِّنْهُ﴾ (in an open space thereof): i.e. a spacious area.
His saying: ﴿وَلَمُلِئْتَ﴾ (and you would have been filled): ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it with the light form, and the people of Medina read ﴿وَلَمُلِئْتَ مِنْهُمْ﴾ with the doubled form. «[Translator's note: both forms are quoted in the text with the same spelling; the doubled reading is لَمُلِّئْتَ.]» This is addressed to Muhammad ﷺ.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿بِوَرِقِكُمْ﴾ (with this silver coin of yours): ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it with the light form, and it is الوَرِق. Some Arabs say الوِرْق, just as one says كَبِد, كِبْدٌ and كَبْدٌ (liver), and كَلِمَةٌ, كَلْمَةٌ and كِلْمَة (word).
His saying ﴿فَلْيَنْظُرْ أَيُّهَآ أَزْكَىٰ﴾ (and let him see which of it is purest): it is said: which is the most lawful slaughtered meat, because they were Magians.

farraa:21-21.t: His saying: ﴿أَعْثَرْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ (We caused [them] to find them): We made (them) manifest and caused (them) to be discovered. Similar is (the verse) in al-Māʾida: ﴿فإن عُثِرَ﴾ (and if it is found): it is discovered. (The singular of الأيقاظ (awake) is يَقِظ and يَقُظ.) «[Translator's note: the text has "الأبقاظ".]»

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ سَبْعَةٌ وَثَامِنُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ﴾ (and they say: seven, and the eighth of them their dog): Ibn ʿAbbās said: they were seven, and the eighth of them was their dog. And Ibn ʿAbbās said: I am among the few of whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿مَّا يَعْلَمُهُمْ إِلاَّ قَلِيلٌ﴾ (none knows them except a few).
Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said to His Prophet, upon him be peace: ﴿فَلاَ تُمَارِ فِيهِمْ﴾ (so do not argue about them), O Muhammad, ﴿إِلاَّ مِرَآءً ظَاهِراً﴾ (except with an obvious argument): except that you tell them about it as a narration.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَسْتَفْتِ فِيهِمْ﴾ (and do not inquire about them) — about the people of the cave — (مِّنْهُمْ) (among them) — of the Christians — (أَحَداً) (anyone). They were two parties who came to him from the people of Najrān: a Jacobite and a Nestorian. The Prophet ﷺ asked them about their number, and he was forbidden (to do so). That is His saying ﴿وَلاَ تَسْتَفْتِ فِيهِمْ مِّنْهُمْ أَحَداً﴾.

farraa:23-24.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَقْولَنَّ لِشَيْءٍ إِنِّي فَاعِلٌ ذٰلِكَ غَداً﴾ (and never say of anything: "I shall do that tomorrow") ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾ (except [adding]: "if Allah wills"): except that you say: "if Allah wills" (and, along with "saying", it may be: and do not say it unless Allah wills), i.e. except what Allah intends.
His saying ﴿وَٱذْكُر رَّبَّكَ إِذَا نَسِيتَ﴾ (and remember your Lord when you forget): Ibn ʿAbbās said: when you swear an oath and forget to make the exception (i.e. to say "if Allah wills"), make the exception whenever you remember, as long as you have not broken the oath.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿ثَلاثَ مِئَةٍ سِنِينَ﴾ (three hundred years) — in genitive construct. «[Translator's note: i.e. the reading ثلاثَ مئةِ سنين without nunation.]» Many readers read (ثَلاثَ مِئَةٍ سِنِينَ) (with nunation), meaning "and they stayed in their cave years", so they make it accusative by the verb.
Some Arabs put السنين in the place of سَنَة (year), and it is then in the position of the genitive for whoever uses the construct. Whoever nunates while meaning the construct sense makes السنين accusative as an explanation (tamyīz (specification)) of the number, like the saying of ʿAntara:
فيها اثنتان وَأربعونَ حَلُوبةً * سُودا كخافية الغُراب الأَسحم
(Among them are forty-two milch camels, black like the inner feathers of the jet-black raven.)
He made (سُوداً), which is a plural, a specification, just as the singular specifies.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿أَبْصِرْ بِهِ وَأَسْمِعْ﴾ (how Seeing is He, and how Hearing!): He means Allah, Blessed and Exalted, like your saying in ordinary speech: أكرم بعبدالله (how noble is ʿAbdallāh!), whose meaning is: ما أكرم عبدالله. Likewise His saying ﴿أَسْمِعْ بِهِمْ وَأَبْصِر﴾: how well they will hear, how well they will see! In anything that has a sense of praise or blame you say: أظرِف به (how witty he is!) and أكرم به; and from (roots with) yāʾ and wāw: أَطْيِبُ به طعاماً (how good it is as food!) and أجْوِد به ثوباً (how fine it is as a garment!). With doubled roots you show the doubling, and assimilation is not permitted, just as dropping the yāʾ or the wāw is not permitted, because its origin is ما أجوده, ما أشدّه and أطيبه, so it was left on that basis. As for أَشدِد به, the doubling appears because of the vowellessness of the lām (third radical) of the verb, and the doubling was kept and not assimilated because it is not put in the dual or feminine: you do not say to two أشِدَّا بِهما, nor to a group أَشِدُّوا بهم. The Arabs allowed themselves to say مدّ in place of امدد only because they say to two مُدَّا and to a group مُدُّوا, so the singular was built on the plural.
His saying ﴿وَلاَ يُشْرِكُ فِي حُكْمِهِ أَحَداً﴾ (and He shares His rule with no one): you make it nominative when it is with yāʾ, in the sense of "and He does not share". Whoever said ﴿لاَ تُشْرِكْ﴾ (do not associate) made it jussive (majzūm), because it is a prohibition.

farraa:27-28.t:
His saying: ﴿مُلْتَحَداً﴾ (a refuge): المُلْتَحد is the place of refuge.
His saying: ﴿بِٱلْغَدَاةِ وَٱلْعَشِيِّ﴾ (morning and evening): Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read (بالغُدْوة والعَشِّى), and I know of no one who read it otherwise «[Translator's note: so the text; the sense is presumably that no one else read بالغدوة.]». The Arabs do not put the alif and lām (the definite article) on غدوة, because it is definite without alif and lām. I heard Abū al-Jarrāḥ say: "I have never seen anything like غُدْوةَ (this morning)", meaning the morning of his day, because it was cold. Do you not see that the Arabs do not put it in the construct; likewise they do not put alif and lām on it. They only say: أتيتكَ غَدَاة الخميس (I came to you on Thursday morning), and do not say: غُدْوةَ الخميس. This is evidence that it is definite.
His saying ﴿وَلاَ تَعْدُ عَيْنَاكَ عَنْهُمْ﴾ (and let not your eyes pass beyond them): the verb belongs to the eyes: let your eyes not turn away from them. This was revealed concerning Salmān and his companions.
His saying ﴿وَكَانَ أَمْرُهُ فُرُطاً﴾ (and whose affair is ever neglect): neglected, obedience having been abandoned in it and disregarded. It is also said that he went to excess in speech, saying: "We are the heads of Muḍar and its nobles", and it was not so. He is ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn. We have mentioned his story in Sūrat al-Anʿām.

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ إِنَّا لاَ نُضِيعُ﴾ (indeed those who believed and did righteous deeds — indeed We will not allow to be lost): the khabar (predicate) of ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ﴾ is in His saying ﴿إِنَّا لاَ نُضِيعُ﴾. It is like the saying of the poet:
إِن الخليفة إنَّ الله سَرْبله * سِرْبالَ مُلْك بها تُزْجَى الخواتيمُ
(Indeed the caliph — indeed Allah has clothed him in the garment of kingship, by which seals are dispatched.)
It is as though, in meaning: "indeed We will not allow to be lost the reward of whoever did good"; so the first statement was left and reliance placed on the second, with the intention of repetition; as He said ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الشَّهْرِ الحَرَامِ﴾ (they ask you about the sacred month), then said ﴿قِتَالٍ فيهِ﴾ (fighting in it), meaning "about fighting in it", by repetition. It may also be that you take ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ﴾ in the manner of a condition (jazāʾ), as you say: "indeed whoever does good, then We will not allow his reward to be lost", so you suppress — «[Translator's note: the text has "ب: فتضمر فتضمَّن", i.e. manuscript B reads فتضمر where the main text has فتضمَّن.]» — the fāʾ in His saying (فإنَّا), and dropping it is permitted. That is the aspect dearest to me. And if you wish you make their khabar come later, as though you said: ﴿إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات أولئك لهم جَنَّات عَدْن﴾ (indeed those who believed and did righteous deeds — those will have gardens of perpetual residence).

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلَعَلَّكَ بَاخِعٌ نَّفْسَكَ﴾ (perhaps you would kill yourself [with grief]): i.e. one who takes your own life out, one who kills himself.
His saying: ﴿إِن لَّمْ يُؤْمِنُواْ﴾ (if they do not believe): you give it kasra when they have not yet believed, with the intention of a condition (jazāʾ); and you give it fatḥa when you mean that it has already happened; like His saying elsewhere: ﴿أَفَنَضْرِبُ عَنْكم الذِّكْرَ صَفْحاً إنْ كُنْتُم﴾ (shall We then turn the Reminder away from you, disregarding you, if you are [a transgressing people]) and ﴿أَنْ كُنْتُمْ﴾ (because you are).
Similar is the poet's saying:
أتجزع أن بان الخلِيطُ المودّع * وحبل الصَّفَا من عَزَّة المتقطع
(Do you grieve because the departing companions have left, and because the rope of pure affection with ʿAzza is cut?)

farraa:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿صَعِيداً﴾ (ground): الصعيد is earth (dust). الجُرُز is that the land has no vegetation in it. One says: جُرِزَت الأرضُ (the land was laid bare), and it is مجرُوزة; and the locusts, or the sheep, or the camels جرَزها (laid it bare), i.e. ate what was on it.

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿أَمْ حَسِبْتَ﴾ (or did you think) addresses Muhammad ﷺ. ﴿أَنَّ أَصْحَابَ ٱلْكَهْفِ﴾ (that the companions of the cave): the cave is the mountain in which they took refuge. الرقيم (al-Raqīm) is a lead tablet on which their lineages, their religion, and what they fled from were written.

farraa:31-31.t:
His saying: ﴿يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيهَا مِنْ أَسَاوِرَ مِن ذَهَبٍ﴾ (they will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold): if you dropped (منْ) from "bracelets", it would be accusative. If you dropped (منْ) from "gold", its accusative would be permitted with some ugliness, because the number of the bracelets is not known; the accusative in the specifier (tamyīz (specification)) is good only when the number is known, as in your saying: عندى جُبَّتان خَزّا (I have two cloaks of silk-wool), وأسواران ذهباً (two bracelets of gold), and ثلاثة أساور ذهبا (three bracelets of gold). If you say: عندى أساور ذهباً without stating their number, it should be with من, because what is specified ought to be of known quantity. Similar is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿وَيُنَزِّلُ مِنَ السماءِ مِنْ جِبَالٍ فِيها مِنْ بَرَد﴾ (and He sends down from the sky, from mountains therein, of hail); the meaning is: in it are mountains of hail, and (من) came in because the mountains are not numbered in the wording. But it is permitted, as though by the mountains and the bracelets you meant "many"; as when someone says: "he has only two rings of gold" and you say: "he has rings of gold (خواتِم ذهباً)", since it is a rejoinder to something of known number. So treat the bracelets and "mountains of hail" in this manner.
As for (يُحَلّون), if someone said يَحْلَون it would be permitted, because the Arabs say: امرأة حالية (an adorned woman), and she حلِيت, so she تحلَى (is adorned), when she wears jewellery; she تحلَى حُلِيّاً and حلْياً.
His saying ﴿نِعْمَ ٱلثَّوَابُ﴾ (excellent is the reward): He did not say نعمت الثواب; and He said ﴿وَحَسُنَتْ مُرْتَفَقاً﴾ (and good is it as a resting place), making the verb feminine according to the sense of "Paradise"; had He made it masculine according to the masculine "resting place" it would have been correct, as He said ﴿وبِئْسَ المِهَادُ﴾ (and wretched is the resting place), ﴿وَبِئْسَ القَرَارُ﴾ (and wretched is the settlement), ﴿وبئس المَصِيرُ﴾ (and wretched is the destination), and as He said ﴿بئْسَ لِلظالِمينَ بَدَلاً﴾ (wretched it is for the wrongdoers as an exchange), meaning Iblīs and his offspring, and He did not say بئسوا.
(بئس) may also be for Iblīs alone. The Arabs keep نعم and بئس singular even when they come after the nouns, so they say: أَمّا قومُك فنِعْمُوا قوماً and نعم قوماً (as for your people, what an excellent people they are), and likewise بئس. Keeping them singular is permitted only because they are not verbs whose (verbal) meaning is sought; they were only brought in to indicate praise and blame. Do you not see that their form is that of فَعَل, but their meaning is not so, and that one does not say from them: يبأس الرجل زيد or ينعم الرجل أخوك. That is why they allowed both plural and singular in the verb. Their counterpart is ﴿عَسَى أَنْ يَكُونُوا خَيْراً مِنْهُمْ﴾ (perhaps they may be better than them); and in the reading of ʿAbdallāh: (عَسَوْا أَنْ يَكُونوا خـَيْراً مِنْهُمْ). Do you not see that you do not say هو يَعْسِى, just as you do not say يَبْأَس.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿كِلْتَا ٱلْجَنَّتَيْنِ آتَتْ أُكُلَهَا﴾ (each of the two gardens produced its fruit): He did not say آتتا (dual). That is because (كلتا) is two whose single one is not used alone; its origin is كُلّ, as you say of three: كلّ. So the rule was that the two should have what the plural has, not that something singular be used for one of them; so its singular (verb) was permitted [104b] «[Translator's note: "104 ب" is a manuscript folio marker.]» on the pattern of كلّ. And its being feminine is permitted because of the feminine marker that appears in كِلْتا. Do likewise with كلتا, كِلاَ and كُلّ when you put them in construct with a definite noun and the verb comes after them: use the plural or the singular. Of the singular is His saying ﴿وكُلُّهُمْ آتِيهِ يَوْمَ القِيَامَةِ فَرْداً﴾ (and all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone), and of the plural ﴿وكُلٌّ أَتَوهُ دَاخِرِين﴾ (and all will come to Him humbled), and (آتوه) likewise. This is frequent in the Qurʾān and in other speech. The poet said:
وكلتاهما قد خُطّ لى فى صَحيفتى * فلا العَيْشُ أهواه ولا الموت أرْوح
(Both of them have been written for me in my record: I do not love life, nor is death more restful.)
The Arabs may use one of كلتا in the singular, meaning by the singular its two. One of them recited to me:
فى كِلت رجليهَا سُلاَمَى واحده * كلتاهما مقرونة بزائده
(In each of her two feet is a single toe-bone; both of them joined to an extra one.)
By كلت he means كلتا.
The Arabs also do this with (أىّ): they make it feminine or masculine while the meaning is feminine. Of that is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿وَمَا تَدْرِى نَفْسٌ بِأَىِّ أَرْضٍ تَمُوتُ﴾ (and no soul knows in which land it will die); in ordinary speech بأيَّة أرض is permitted. Similar is ﴿فى أَىِّ صُورة﴾ (in whatever form); in ordinary speech في أيَّة صورة is permitted. The poet said:
بأىّ بلاء أمْ بأيَّة نعمة * يقدَّم قبلى مُسلم والمُهَلَّب
(By what trial, or by what favour, are Muslim and al-Muhallab put ahead of me?)
And أيّتهُما قال ذاك (which of the two [fem.] said [masc.] that) is permitted, though وقالت ذاكَ is better. You use the masculine although you have added the hāʾ, imagining the hāʾ to be absent, since ﴿بأىّ أرضٍ تَمُوتُ﴾ is permitted for the feminine. Likewise you may say of two feminines: كلاهما and كلتاهما. The poet said:
كلا عقِبيه قد تشعّبَ رَأسُهَا * من الضرب فى جَنْبَىْ ثَفَالٍ مباشر
(Both his heels — their tips have split from striking the flanks of a sluggish camel, kicking it directly.)
الثفال: the slow camel.
If someone says: "You permitted the singular with (كلتا) only because one of its two is not used alone; so do you permit الاثنتان قام, using the singular, and الاثنان قام, since no singular of it is used alone?", I say: الاثنان (two) is built on a singular, whereas (كِلاَ) is not built on a singular. Do you not see that your saying قام عبدُالله كلُّه (ʿAbdallāh stood, all of him) is wrong; and that you find the meaning of "two" built on a singular, like the meaning of three and higher numbers; and only الاثنان قاما and الاثنتان قامَتَا (in the dual) is permitted.
It is in the reading of ʿAbdallāh:
* كُلّ الجنتين آتى أُكُله *
and its meaning is: everything of the fruit of the two gardens produced its fruit. Had he meant the sum of the two, and not all the fruit, only كلتاهما would be permitted; do you not see that you do not say: قامت المرأتان كلهما (the two women stood, all of them), because (كل) is not suitable for one of two women, whereas it is suitable for one of two gardens. So judge by these two cases everything that is divisible into parts, whether it can be portioned or not.
His saying ﴿وَفَجَّرْنَا خِلالَهُمَا نَهَراً﴾ (and We caused a river to gush forth within them): it may be asked: how is the doubled form permitted when the river is only one? I say: because the river extends, so that the gushing became as though it were throughout the whole of it; so the light and the heavy forms are both permitted in it. Similar is ﴿حتَّى تَفْجُرَ لَنَا مِنَ الأَرْضِ يَنْبُوعاً﴾ (until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth), read with the heavy and the light form.

farraa:34-34.t: His saying: ﴿وَكَانَ لَهُ ثَمَرٌ﴾ (and he had fruit): Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: al-Muʿallā ibn Hilāl al-Juʿfī told me, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, who said: whatever in the Qurʾān is ثُمُر with ḍamma means wealth, and whatever is ثَمَر with fatḥa is from fruits.

farraa:36-36.t: His saying: ﴿خَيْراً مِّنْهَا مُنْقَلَباً﴾ (better than this as a return) refers back to the garden. In some of the codices of the people of Medina it is (منْهُما مُنْقَلَباً) (than the two), referring back to the two gardens.

farraa:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿لَّٰكِنَّاْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ رَبِّي﴾ (but as for me, He is Allah, my Lord): its meaning is: لكن أنا هو الله ربّى (but I — He is Allah, my Lord). The hamza of the alif of أنا was dropped, and the expression was used frequently, so the nūn of (أنا) was assimilated into the nūn of (لكن). Some Arabs say: أنا قلت ذاك (I said that) with the full alif, so it was read لكنّا according to that dialect; and the alif was kept in the codex for both dialects, just as they said رأيت يزيدا (I saw Yazīd) and قواريرا (flasks), the alif being kept in both in both usages when you pause. In other than the Qurʾān it is permitted to pause on أنا without alif. Some Arabs say, when pausing: أَنَهْ, and this is in a good dialect; it is in upper Tamīm and lower Qays. Abū Tharwān recited to me:
وترميننى بالطّرْف أىْ أنت مذنب * وتقلِيننى لكنّ إيّاكَ لا أَقلى
(You cast glances at me, meaning "you are at fault", and you hate me — but I, I do not hate you.)
He means: لكِنْ أنا إيّاك لا أَقلى; he dropped the hamza, so it became like a single word. Al-Kisāʾī claimed that he heard the Arabs say لكنَّ والله, meaning لكن أنا والله (but I, by Allah). And al-Kisāʾī said: I heard some Arabs say إنَّ قائم, meaning إنْ أنا قائم (I am not standing); he dropped the hamza and assimilated, so it is a counterpart of لكن.

farraa:39-39.t:
His saying: ﴿مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾ (what Allah wills): ما is in the position of the nominative. If you wish, you make it nominative by suppressing (هو), meaning: هو ما شاء الله (it is what Allah willed). And if you wish, you suppress ما شاء الله كان (what Allah willed came to be), dropping (كان); and then the position of (ما) is accusative by شاء, because the verb falls on it. Dropping the answer (jawāb) is permitted, as He said ﴿فإنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ أَنْ تَبْتَغىَ نَفَقَا فىِ الأرْضِ أَوْ سُلَّماً فىِ السَّماءِ﴾ (and if you are able to seek a tunnel into the earth or a ladder into the sky…), which has no answer because its meaning is known.
His saying: ﴿إِن تَرَنِ أَنَاْ أَقَلَّ مِنكَ﴾ (if you see me less than you): (أنا), when you make (أقلَّ) accusative, is an ʿimād (support pronoun); and when you make (أقل) nominative it is a noun (i.e. mubtadaʾ (subject)). Reading with both is permitted.

farraa:40-40.t: His saying: ﴿صَعِيداً زَلَقاً﴾ (slippery ground): الزلَق is earth with no vegetation on it, burnt and decayed.

farraa:41-41.t: [His saying:] ﴿مَآؤُهَا غَوْراً﴾ (its water sunken): the Arabs say: ماء غَوْر (sunken water), ماءان غَوْر (two sunken waters), and مِياه غوْر (sunken waters), with the singular in every case.

farraa:42-43.t:
His saying: ﴿خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا﴾ (fallen down upon its trellises): upon its roofs.
His saying: ﴿وَلَمْ تَكُن لَّهُ فِئَةٌ يَنصُرُونَهُ﴾ (and he had no party to help him): He referred (the plural verb) to the men. Had it been said تَنْصره, referring to the party (feminine) — as He said ﴿(فِئَةٌ) تُقَاتِلُ فىِ سَبيلِ اللهِ وَأُخْرَى كَافِرَةٌ﴾ (one party fighting in the way of Allah and another disbelieving) — it would have been permitted.

farraa:44-44.t: His saying: ﴿هُنَالِكَ ٱلْوَلاَيَةُ لِلَّهِ ٱلْحَقُّ﴾ (there, the authority is Allah's, the True): (الحقّ) is nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of (الولاية). In the reading of Ubayy: (هُنَالِكَ ٱلْوَلاَيَةُ ٱلْحَقُّ لِلَّه) (there, the true authority is Allah's). If you wish you make it genitive, making it a naʿt of (الله). الوِلاية is sovereignty. Had you made (الحقّ) accusative in the sense of "truly" (حقّا), it would have been correct.

farraa:45-45.t:
His saying: ﴿تَذْرُوهُ ٱلرِّياحُ﴾ (the winds scatter it): from ذَرَوت, and ذَرَيْت is a dialect form; it is thus in the reading of ʿAbdallāh: (تَذْرِيه الريح). Had a reader read (تُذْريه الريح), from أذريت, i.e. it throws it down, that would be a valid aspect. Al-Mufaḍḍal recited to me:
فقلت له صوِّب ولا تجهَدَنَّهُ * فيُذرِكَ منْ أُخْرى القطاةِ فتَزْلَقِ
(I said to him: go gently and do not tire it out, lest it throw you off the back of its croup and you slip.)
You say: أذريت الرجل عن الدابَّة and عن البعير, i.e. I threw him off the riding animal or the camel.

farraa:46-46.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلْبَاقِيَاتُ ٱلصَّالِحَاتُ﴾ (and the enduring good deeds): it is said they are the five prayers, and it is said they are: Subḥān Allāh, al-ḥamdu li-llāh, lā ilāha illā Allāh and Allāhu akbar.
His saying: ﴿وَخَيْرٌ أَمَلاً﴾ (and better for hope): (he says: the best of what is hoped for); and hope for a good deed is better than hope for an evil deed.

farraa:47-47.t:
His saying ﴿وَيَوْمَ نُسَيِّرُ ٱلْجِبَالَ﴾ (and the day We will set the mountains moving), and His saying: ﴿وَتَرَى ٱلأَرْضَ بَارِزَةً﴾ (and you will see the earth laid bare): he says: We brought its people out from its belly. It is also said: the mountains were moved away from it, so it all became exposed, no part of it concealing another.
His saying: ﴿فَلَمْ نُغَادِرْ مِنْهُمْ﴾ (and We will not leave behind any of them): this is the reading (and had it been read "ولم نغْدِرْ" it would have been correct); their meaning is one. One says: ما أغدرت منهم أحداً and ما غادرت (I left none of them behind). One of them recited to me:
هل لك والعائض منهم عائِض * فى هجمة يغدرمنها القابض * سُدْسا ورُبعا تحتها فرائض *
(Would you like — and the one who gives in exchange is giving in exchange — a herd of camels from which the receiver leaves behind sudus and rubʿ camels, with obligatory-alms camels beneath them?)
Al-Farrāʾ said: sudus and rubʿ are among the ages of camels.

farraa:50-50.t: His saying: ﴿فَفَسَقَ عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهِ﴾ (and he departed from the command of his Lord): i.e. he went out from obedience to his Lord. The Arabs say: فَسَقت الرُّطَبة (the fresh date came out) of its (skin) and its peel, because it comes out of it. It seems the mouse was called فُوَيْسِقة only because it comes out of its hole upon people.

farraa:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا بَيْنَهُم مَّوْبِقاً﴾ (and We will put between them a place of ruin): it is said: We made their ties in this world (مَوْبَقاً), he says: a cause of destruction for them in the Hereafter. It is also said that it is a valley in Hell.

farraa:53-53.t: His saying: ﴿فَظَنُّوۤاْ أَنَّهُمْ مُّوَاقِعُوهَا﴾ (and they will think that they are to fall into it): i.e. they will know.

farraa:55-55.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا مَنَعَ ٱلنَّاسَ أَن يُؤْمِنُوۤاْ﴾ (and nothing has prevented the people from believing): it is said that "the people" here is in the sense of a single man. His saying ﴿إِلاَّ أَن تَأْتِيَهُمْ سُنَّةُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ﴾ (except that the way of the former peoples should come to them): أن is in the position of the nominative. His saying ﴿سُنَّةُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ﴾: he says: Our way in destroying the nations that denied. His saying ﴿أَوْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ قُبُلاً﴾ (or the punishment should come to them before their eyes): openly. (قِبَلاً) may have this meaning; and (قُبُلاً) may be as though it were a plural of قَبِيل — and قُبُل — i.e. punishment of different kinds, one following another.

farraa:58-58.t:
His saying: ﴿لَّن يَجِدُواْ مِن دُونِهِ مَوْئِلاٍ﴾ (they will never find besides it an escape): (الموئل is the place of escape), and it is the place of refuge; in meaning they are one. The Arabs say: إنه ليوائل إلى موضعه, meaning: he goes to his place and his stronghold.
The poet said:
لا وألت نفسك خلَّيتها * للعامريّين ولم تُكْلَم
(May your soul find no escape! You abandoned it to the ʿĀmirīs and you were not even wounded.)
(He means: may it not be saved.)

farraa:59-59.t:
His saying: ﴿لِمَهْلِكِهِم مَّوْعِداً﴾ (for their destruction an appointed time): he says: for Our destroying them, (موعداً) a fixed term. ʿĀṣim read (لمَهْلَكهِمْ), with fatḥa on the mīm and the lām; and (لمهِلِكهم) «[Translator's note: so the text; i.e. لِمَهْلِكِهِم.]» with kasra on the lām is permitted, building it on هَلَك يَهْلِك. Whoever wants the noun (of place/time) from a verb whose imperfect has kasra on the ʿayn gives mafʿil kasra; whoever wants the maṣdar (verbal noun) gives the ʿayn fatḥa — like المضرِب and المضرَب, المَدِبّ and المَدَبّ, المفِرّ and المَفَرّ. When the yafʿal (imperfect) has fatḥa on the ʿayn, the Arabs prefer fatḥa on it in mafʿal, whether noun or maṣdar. Sometimes they give the ʿayn kasra in mafʿil when they mean the noun by it; some of them said ﴿مَجْمِعَ البَحْرَيْنِ﴾ (the meeting place of the two seas), and that is the analogical form, though it is rare.
When the yafʿul has ḍamma on the ʿayn, like يدخل and يخرج, the Arabs prefer fatḥa on the ʿayn in both the noun and the maṣdar from it — except certain nouns to which they have made kasra on the ʿayn in mafʿil obligatory. Among them: المسجِد (mosque), المطلِع (place of rising), المغرِب (west), المشرِق (east), المسقِط (place of falling), المفرِق (parting of the hair), المجزِر (slaughter place), المسكِن (dwelling), المَرْفِق from رَفَق يَرْفُق, المنسِك from نَسَك يَنْسُك, and المنبت.
So they made kasra the mark of the noun and fatḥa the mark of the maṣdar. Sometimes some Arabs give it fatḥa (in the noun); مسكِن and مسكَن have both been read. We have heard المسجِد and المسجَد when they meant the noun, and المطلَع and المطلِع. Fatḥa (naṣb) is permitted in all of it; even if you have not heard it, do not reject it if it comes.
Whatever is from (roots with final) yāʾ and wāw, like دعوت and قضيت, its mafʿal has fatḥa, whether noun or maṣdar — except المأقِى (the inner corner) of the eye, for the Arabs gave this word kasra. Some Arabs call the shelter of camels مَأْوِى. These two are rare. They refrained from (giving kasra to the ʿayn) with yāʾ and wāw only because the yāʾ and the wāw disappear in pause on account of the nunation that attaches, so they turned it into alif, since that does not drop in pause.
When the mafʿal is from كال يكيل (to measure) and similar verbs, the noun from it has kasra and the maṣdar fatḥa; of that is مال مَمِيلا and مَمَالا: you take the kasra to the nouns and the fatḥa to the maṣdars. Had you given both fatḥa, or both kasra, in the maṣdar and the noun, it would be permitted. The Arabs say المعاش (livelihood), and they have said المعيش. Ruʾba ibn al-ʿAjjāj said:
إليك اشكو شدّة المعيش * ومرّ أعوام نتَفْن ريشى * نتف الحُبَارَى عن قَرَا رَهِيشِ *
(To You I complain of the hardness of living [106a] «[Translator's note: "106 ا" is a manuscript folio marker.]», and of the passing of years that have plucked my feathers, as the bustard is plucked from a lean back.)
القَرَا: the back. And another said:
أنا الرجل الذى قد عبتموهُ * ومَا فيكم لَعَيّاب مَعَاب
(I am the man whom you have found fault with, yet there is nothing in you for a fault-finder to fault.)
Similar are مَسَار and مَسِير; and whatever resembles it is like it.
When the yafʿal from (roots with middle) yāʾ and wāw has fatḥa, like يخاف and يهاب, the noun and the maṣdar from it both have fatḥa, like المخاف and المهاب.
Whatever is from wāw with ḍamma, like يقوم, يقول, يعود, يقود and the like, the noun and the maṣdar in it both have fatḥa. They gave it fatḥa even when intending the noun, and did not give it kasra as المَغْرِب was given kasra, only because they disliked the wāw turning into yāʾ, so that the wāw would be confused with the yāʾ.
Whatever begins with wāw, like وزنت, ورثت and وجِلت, its mafʿil, whether noun or maṣdar, has kasra; as in His saying ﴿أَنْ لَنْ نَجْعَلَ لَكُمْ مَوْعِداً﴾ (that We would never make for you an appointment). Likewise يَوْحَل and يَوْحَل «[Translator's note: so the text, the word repeated; perhaps يَوْجَل and يَوْحَل.]»: the mafʿil from both has kasra (in both aspects). Al-Kisāʾī claimed that he heard مَوْجَل and مَوْحَل. Al-Farrāʾ said: and I heard «[Translator's note: the text has "ويمعت", evidently وسمعت.]» موضَع. They gave kasra to what begins with wāw only because when the verb in it has fatḥa it is of two kinds: as for the transitive, its wāw drops, like وَزَن يزِنُ; and the intransitive keeps its wāw in yafʿal. The maṣdars are the same for the transitive and the intransitive, so they made no distinction in their two maṣdars; distinctions are only in faʿala/yafʿilu.
Whatever has hamza is with fatḥa in both cases. It is as though they built it on yafʿal, because what has hamza as its lām (third radical) comes with fatḥa on the ʿayn, from faʿala and from faʿila. If you say: "What if they gave it kasra intending the noun, as they gave kasra to مجمِع?", I say: it has not come. It is as though they treated the hamzated (root) like the yāʾ and the wāw, because the hamza may be dropped, so it joins them.
Whatever mafʿal is derived from afʿaltu (the fourth form), you may give the mīm of its noun and its maṣdar ḍamma; and you may produce it according to its original form before the alif was added to it. So you say: أخرجته مُخْرجاً and مَخْرجاً (I brought him out), and أنزلته مُنْزَلاً and مَنْزِلاً (I lodged him). It has been read: ﴿أَنْزِلْنِى مُنْزَلاَ مُبَارَكاً﴾ (land me at a blessed landing place), ﴿وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ المُنْزِلِينِ﴾ (and You are the best to accommodate [us]), and ﴿مَنْزِلا﴾.
Whatever is an instrument with which work is done, like المِرْوحة (fan), المِطرقة (hammer) and the like, with or without the hāʾ (tāʾ marbūṭa), has kasra on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn; like المِدْرع, المِلحف, المِطرق and the like. However, they said: المَطهرة and المِطهرة (vessel for purification), المَرقاة and المِرقاة (ladder), المَسقاة and المِسقاة (watering vessel). Whoever gives it kasra likens it to the instrument with which work is done; whoever gives it fatḥa says: this is a place in which something is done, so he made it different and gave the mīm fatḥa. Do you not see that the fan and the like are instruments worked with, while the purification vessel and the ladder stay in their places and do not move, and things are done on them.
Whatever is a feminine maṣdar, the Arabs may give its ʿayn ḍamma; like المقدُرة and the like. They do not do that in a masculine without the hāʾ, because when the hāʾ is added the pattern of faʿala/yafʿalu falls away from it and it becomes a different noun, whereas mafʿal is built on yafʿal. So they avoided ḍamma in mafʿal, because the form of yafʿul that requires ḍamma is (like) كَرُم يكرُم; they disliked imposing a ḍamma on the ʿayn of [106b] «[Translator's note: "106 ب" is a manuscript folio marker.]» mafʿal, lest the ignorant think there is a binding distinction in mafʿal as the distinctions bind faʿila/yafʿalu; so it was given fatḥa, with the intention of mixing it with the maṣdars of transitive verbs. As for the poet's saying:
* لِيوم رَوْعٍ أو فَعَال مَكْرُم *
(for a day of terror, or a deed of nobility)
it is a plural of مَكْرُمة: مكْرُم. Similar is another's saying:
بثين الزمى لا إنّه إن لزِمته * على كثرة الواشين أىُّ مَعُونِ
(Buthayna, hold fast to "no", for if you hold to it, despite the many slanderers, what a help it is!)
He meant the plural of معونة. Al-Kisāʾī used to say: they are two rare mafʿul (forms) on which no analogy is made; he took a certain view, but I find the first view more fitting for Arabic than what he said. The yāʾ may be changed into wāw in it, so one says:
وكنت إذا جارى دعا لَمضُوفةٍ * أشمِّر حتى يَنْصُف الساق مئزرى
(When my neighbour called out because of a calamity, I would tuck up my garment until my waist-wrap reached half my shin.)
He made it mafʿula, though it is from yāʾ, and turned it into wāw because of the ḍamma before it, as they said: قد سُور به.
In certain words the Arabs gave both the mīm and the ʿayn ḍamma, and (in others) gave the mīm and the ʿayn both kasra. Among those whose ʿayn and mīm they gave ḍamma is their saying: مُكْحُلة (kohl container), مُسْعُط (snuff-tube), مُدْهُن (oil flask) and مُدُقّ (pestle). Among those whose mīm and ʿayn they gave kasra: مِنْخِر (nostril) and مِنْتِن (stinking). Among those to which they added a yāʾ for the kasra and a wāw for the ḍamma: مِسكين, مِنديل and مِنطق; and with wāw, like مُغْفُور and مُغْثُور, which is (the gum) that falls on the thumām plant; and the nostril is called مُنخور — these are Ṭayyiʾ. Those who gave ḍamma to its beginning and its ʿayn likened the mīm to a radical letter, as though it were fuʿlūl; likewise those who gave kasra to the mīm and the ʿayn likened it to filʿīl «[Translator's note: so the text; probably فِعْلِيل is meant.]» and fiʿlil.
Whatever has an augment mīm that you add to a quadriliteral verb — one whose triliteral (root) has received some augment — the mīm in it is with ḍamma in the active participle, the passive participle and the maṣdar. Of that is your saying: رجل مُستضرِبٌ (and مُستضرَبٌ), مستطعِم and مستطعَم; مستطعَم — with fatḥa — may be a maṣdar or a man (passive participle). Likewise المضارِب is the agent, and المضارَب — with fatḥa — is a maṣdar or a man. «[Translator's note: the text has "المضاربَ" in both places; the kasra/fatḥa distinction is evidently intended.]» All augmented forms are on this pattern without exception, and there is no difference about it among dialects or otherwise — except that some Arabs, and they are few, say of المتكبِّر (the arrogant): متكبَّر, as though they built it on يتكبَّر. It is of the dialect of the Anṣār, and it is not something to be built upon. Al-Farrāʾ said: I have been told that some Arabs give the mīm kasra in this type when there is assimilation, saying هم المِطَّوِّعة (the volunteers), and المِسَّمِع for المُستمع (the listener); they are of the Anṣār, and it is among the rejected (usages). The Arabs said مَوْهَب, making it a coined noun not on (any verbal) pattern, and مَوْكَل as a coined noun. Among them is مَوحَد, because they did not mean the maṣdar of وَحَد; it was only made a noun in the sense of "one by one", like مَثْنَى, ثُلاَث and رُبَاع. As for their saying مَزْيد and مَزْوَد, they too are two different nouns not on the verbal pattern. In such divergence you may give fatḥa to what would properly have kasra when it resembles some patterns, and give ḍamma or kasra to what has fatḥa when you direct it toward one of the patterns of their nouns — as مَعفور «[Translator's note: above it was spelled مُغْفُور.]» was said for (the gum) that falls on the thumām, its mīm being an augment, and it was likened to fuʿlūl; and as the Arabs said (of المصير (intestine), which is from صِرت, مُصْران for the plural), and of مَسيل الماء (water-course), which is mafʿil, مُسْلان for the plural; so they likened mafʿil to faʿīl. Do you not see that they said سُؤته مسائية (I grieved him), whereas it is only مساءة on the pattern mafʿala, and a yāʾ was added at its end, as it is added to faʿāla, as in كراهة and كراهية (dislike), and طَبَانة and طبانِيَة (acuteness).

farraa:60-60.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِفَتَاهُ لاۤ أَبْرَحُ﴾ (and when Moses said to his servant: "I will not cease"): He means: I will not cease (لا أزال) until I reach; He did not mean: I will not leave my place. His saying: ﴿فَلَنْ أَبْرحَ الأَرْضَ حَتَّى يَأْذَنَ لِى أَبىِ﴾ (so I will never leave the land until my father permits me) is not in the sense of أزال; this is staying (in a place). His saying ﴿لَنْ نبْرَحَ عَليْهِ عَاكِفِينَ﴾ (we will not cease being devoted to it): we will not cease being devoted to it. Similar to it are ما فتئت and ما فتأت — a dialect form — and لا أفتأ أذكرك (I do not cease remembering you). His saying ﴿تَاللهِ تَفْتَأُ تَذْكُرُ يُوسُفَ﴾ (by Allah, you will not cease remembering Joseph): its meaning is: you will not cease remembering Joseph. تزال, أفتأ and أبرح, when in this meaning, occur only with a negation (jaḥd), overt or suppressed. As for the overt, you see it in the Qurʾān: ﴿وَلاَ يَزَالُونَ مُخْتَلِفين﴾ (and they will not cease to differ), ﴿وَلاَ يَزَالُ الذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ (and those who disbelieve will not cease), ﴿فَمَا زَالَتْ تِلْكَ دَعْوَاهُمُ﴾ (and that cry of theirs did not cease), and likewise ﴿لاۤ أَبْرَحُ﴾. That in which the negation is suppressed is the saying of Allah (تَفْتَأُ), whose meaning is: لا تفتأ — you will not cease remembering Joseph. Similar is the saying of the poet:
فَلاَ وأَبىِ دَهْمَاءَ زَالَتْ عزِيزةً * عَلَى قومها ما فتَّل الزَّنْدَ قَادِحُ
(No, by Dahmāʾ's father, she will not cease to be dear to her people as long as a fire-maker twirls the fire-stick.)
And likewise the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
فقلت يمينُ الله أبرح قاعداً * ولو قطعُوا رَأسى لديكِ وأوصَالى
(I said: by the oath of Allah, I will not stop sitting here, even if they cut off my head and limbs at your side.)
His saying: ﴿أَوْ أَمْضِيَ حُقُباً﴾ (or I continue for a long period): الحُقُب in the dialect of Qays is a year; and the commentary has come that it is eighty years. As for His saying: ﴿مَجْمَعَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ﴾ (the meeting place of the two seas), it is the sea of Persia and (the sea of) the Byzantines. He was called the young man (فتى) of Moses only because he kept close to him, taking knowledge from him; he is Joshua son of Nun (Yūshaʿ ibn Nūn).

farraa:61-61.t:
His saying: ﴿نَسِيَا حُوتَهُمَا﴾ (they forgot their fish): only Joshua forgot it, but He attributed it to both of them, as He said ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا الُّلؤلُؤ وَالمَرْجانُ﴾ (from both of them come forth pearl and coral), though they come forth only from the salt (sea), not the fresh. His saying ﴿فَٱتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُ فِي ٱلْبَحْرِ سَرَباً﴾ (and it took its course into the sea, burrowing): it was salted; when it came to life through the water from the spring that touched it and fell into the sea, its path in the sea froze, so it was like a tunnel.
His saying: ﴿فَٱتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُ﴾ (and it took its course).
He says: Moses took the course of the fish ﴿فىِ البَحْرِ عَجَباً﴾ (into the sea, amazingly).
Then he said, when he told him the story of the fish.

farraa:64-64.t: His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ مَا كُنَّا نَبْغِ﴾ (that is what we were seeking): i.e. this is what we were seeking.

farraa:70-70.t: His saying: ﴿حَتَّىٰ أُحْدِثَ لَكَ مِنْهُ ذِكْراً﴾ (until I make to you mention of it): he says: until I am the one who asks you «[Translator's note: so the text; the sense is presumably "until I am the one who tells you".]».

farraa:71-71.t: His saying: ﴿لِيَغْرَقَ أَهْلَهَا﴾ (so that its people would drown): Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Ḥasan read it with the nominative and with yāʾ «[Translator's note: i.e. لِيَغْرَقَ أَهْلُها; the text quotes the verse with أهلَها.]», and the rest of the people read it ﴿لِتُغْرِقَ أَهْلَهَا﴾ (to drown its people).

farraa:73-73.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ تُؤَاخِذْنِي بِمَا نَسِيتُ﴾ (do not blame me for what I forgot): Abū al-ʿAbbās told us: Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Yaḥyā «[Translator's note: the text has "يحينى".]» ibn al-Muhallab — who was among the most excellent of the people of Kufa — told me, from a man, from al-Minhāl, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb al-Anṣārī, who said: he did not forget; rather, it was a form of indirect speech (maʿārīḍ al-kalām).
His saying ﴿وَلاَ تُرْهِقْنِي﴾ (and do not cover me): he says: do not hurry me.

farraa:74-74.t: His saying: ﴿أَقَتَلْتَ نَفْساً (زَكِيَّةً)﴾ (have you killed a pure soul?): he passed by a boy who had committed no offence that Moses could see, and killed him. His saying (زَكِيَّة): ʿĀṣim, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Ḥasan read it (زكيّةِ), and the people of the Ḥijāz and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān «[Translator's note: the text has "أبو الرحمن".]» al-Sulamī read it (زَاكية), with alif. It is like His saying ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا قُلُوبَهُمْ قاسِيةً﴾ (and We made their hearts hard) and (وقَسِيَّة).

farraa:76-76.t: His saying: ﴿فَلاَ تُصَاحِبْنِي﴾ (then do not keep me as a companion) and ﴿فَلاَ تَصْحَبْنِى﴾ (do not accompany me): (i.e.) your self (should not accompany me), and do not you accompany me. All of that is correct, and Allah is praised.

farraa:77-77.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأَبَوْاْ أَن يُضَيِّفُوهُمَا﴾ (but they refused to host them): they asked them for hospitality — to be taken as guests — and they did not do it. Had it been read (أَنْ يُضِيفُوهُمَا), it would have been correct. It is said that the town was Antioch. [His saying] ﴿يُرِيدُ أَن يَنقَضَّ﴾ (wanting to collapse): it may be asked: how can a wall want to collapse? That is part of the speech of the Arabs, that they say: "the wall wants to fall". Similar is the saying of Allah ﴿وَلَمَّا سَكَتَ عَنْ مُوسَى الغَضَبُ﴾ (and when the anger fell silent in Moses), whereas anger does not fall silent (it is only its owner who falls silent); its meaning is only: it subsided. And His saying: ﴿فَإذا عَزَمَ الأَمْرُ﴾ (and when the matter is resolved) — [and] it is only the people concerned who resolve the matter. The poet said:
إن دهرا يلفُّ شملى بجُمْلٍ * لزمان يَهُمُّ بالإِحْسَانِ
(A time that gathers my fortunes together with Juml is surely a time that intends kindness.)
And another said:
شكا إلى جملى طول السُّرى * صبراً جميلاً فكلاَنا مبتَلَى
(My camel complained to me of the long night journey: "Beautiful patience! Both of us are being tried.")
The camel did not complain; it was spoken of as though, had it spoken, it would have said that. Likewise the saying of ʿAntara:
فازوَرَّ من وَقْع القَنَا بِلَبَانه * وشكا إلىَّ بعَبْرة وتَحْمحُمِ
(He swerved from the blows of the spears on his chest, and complained to me with a tear and a whinny.)
(يَنْقَاض) has been mentioned (as a reading) for the wall. الانقياض is a crack along the length of a wall, in the stone lining of a well, and in a man's tooth; one says: انقاضت سِنُّهُ when it cracks lengthwise. Then Moses said: "If you had wished [you would not have set it up until they gave us hospitality; that is the wage. And Mujāhid read]: ﴿لو شئت لتَخِذْتَ عَلَيْهِ أجْراً﴾ (if you had wished, you could have taken a wage for it)." Al-Qanānī recited to me:
* تَخِذَهَا سُرِّيَّةً تُقَعِّده *
(He took her as a concubine who would serve him.)
Its origin is اتّخذ, (on the pattern) iftaʿala.

farraa:78-78.t: His saying: ﴿هَـٰذَا فِرَاقُ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنِكَ﴾ (this is parting between me and you): [had you made the second (بين) accusative it would have been correct, imagining that it was (فراق ما بينى وبينك) (the parting of what is between me and you)].

farraa:79-79.t: His saying: ﴿وَكَانَ وَرَآءَهُم مَّلِكٌ﴾ (and behind them was a king): he says: ahead of them was a king. It is like His saying ﴿مِنْ وَرَائه جَهَنَّم﴾ (behind him is Hell), i.e. it is in front of him. You may not say of a man behind you: "he is in front of you", nor of a man in front of you: "he is behind you". That is permitted only with times — days, nights and time in general — so that you say: "behind you is severe cold" and "in front of you is severe cold"; because you are behind it, it is permitted, since it is something that is coming: it is as though, when it catches up with you, it is behind you, and as though, when you reach it, it is in front of you. That is why both aspects are permitted.

farraa:80-80.t: His saying: ﴿فَخَشِينَآ﴾ (and we feared): and we knew. In the reading of Ubayy it is (فخاف ربُّك أَنْ يُرهِقَهُمَا) (so your Lord feared that he would overburden them), in the sense: your Lord knew. It is like His saying ﴿إلاَّ أنْ يَخَافا﴾ (unless they both fear); he said: unless they both know and think. Fear and thinking are taken in the sense of knowledge.

farraa:81-81.t: His saying: ﴿خَيْراً مِّنْهُ زَكَـاةً﴾ (better than him in purity): in righteousness. ﴿وَأَقْرَبَ رُحْماً﴾ (and nearer in mercy): he says: more likely that they would be shown mercy through him. It (رُحْم) is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of رحمت.

farraa:82-82.t:
His saying: ﴿كَنزٌ لَّهُمَا﴾ (a treasure belonging to them): it is said: knowledge.
His saying ﴿رَحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ﴾ (as a mercy from your Lord) is accusative: He did that as a mercy from Him. Every verbal noun «[Translator's note: the text has "فعل" (verb); a maṣdar is evidently meant.]» that you see explaining the statement before it is accusative. You recognise it by seeing that هو (it, masc.) or هى (it, fem.) would fit before the maṣdar; when they are dropped, the maṣdar is joined to the speech before it and so is made accusative. As in His saying ﴿فَضْلاً مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ (as a bounty from your Lord), and His saying ﴿إنَّكَ لَمِنَ المُرْسَلِينَ عَلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيِم تَنْزِيلَ العزِيزِ الرَّحيم﴾ (indeed you are among the messengers, on a straight path — a revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful); its meaning is: you are among the messengers, and it is a revelation of the Mighty — ﴿وهذا تنزيل العزيز الرحيم﴾ (and this is a revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful). Likewise His saying ﴿فِيهَا يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ أَمْراً مِنْ عِنْدِنَا﴾ (in it every wise matter is made distinct — a command from Us); its meaning is: the distinguishing in it is a command from Us. When you drop what would make the maṣdar nominative, it is joined to what precedes it and is made accusative.

farraa:85-85.t: His saying: ﴿فَأَتْبَعَ سَبَباً﴾ (so he followed a way): it has been read (فأتْبَع) and (اتَّبَع); أَتْبَع is better than اتَّبع, because اتَّبعت الرجل is (said) when he is travelling and you travel behind him; and when you say أَتبعته, with the disjunctive alif (hamzat al-qaṭʿ), it is as though you went after him (to catch up).

farraa:86-86.t:
His saying: ﴿حَمِئَةٍ﴾ (muddy): Abū al-ʿAbbās told us: Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Ḥibbān told me, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: (حَمِئَةٍ) — he said: it sets in a black spring. And Ibn ʿAbbās read it so. Abū al-ʿAbbās told us: Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna told me, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read (حَمِئَةٍ). Abū al-ʿAbbās told us: Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz told me, from Mughīra, from Mujāhid, that Ibn al-Zubayr read (حَامِيَة) (hot). Some of the elders mentioned, from Khaṣīf, from Abū ʿUbayda, (that Ibn Masʿūd read) (حَامِيَةٍ).
His saying ﴿إِمَّآ أَن تُعَذِّبَ وَإِمَّآ أَن تَتَّخِذَ فِيهِمْ حُسْناً﴾ (either you punish, or else you adopt among them goodness): the position of both instances of أن is accusative. Had you made it nominative it would be correct, i.e. "it is only either this or this". One of the Arabs recited to me:
فسيرا فإمَّا حاجةٌ تقضيانها * وإما مَقِيل صالح وصديق
(So travel on, you two: it will be either a need you fulfil, or a good resting place and a friend.)
[108a] «[Translator's note: "108 ا" is a manuscript folio marker.]» Had His saying ﴿فَإمَّا مَنّاً بَعْدُ وَإِمَّا فِدَاءَ﴾ (then either a favour afterwards or ransom) been in the nominative, it would have been correct; the Arabs begin afresh with إمّا… وإمّا. One of Banū ʿUkl recited to me:
ومن لا يزل يستودع الناسَ مالَه * تَرِبْهُ على بعض الخطوب الودائِعُ
ترى الناس إمّا جاعلوه وقاية * لمالهُم أو تاركوه فضائع
(Whoever keeps entrusting his wealth to people, the deposits will trouble him in some misfortune: you see people either making it a shield for their own wealth, or leaving it, so that it is lost.)
وقايةً and وِقَاءَهُم «[Translator's note: these appear to be variant readings for the verse.]». The accusative is on the basis of "do with us this or this", and the nominative on the basis of "it is this or this".

farraa:88-88.t: His saying: ﴿فَلَهُ جَزَآءً ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ﴾ (he will have the best as reward): i.e. he will have the reward of the best; you make الجزاء accusative as an explanation (tafsīr, i.e. tamyīz (specification)), and this is of what I have explained to you. His saying ﴿جَزَآءً ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ﴾ (read) in the construct «[Translator's note: i.e. the reading جزاءُ الحسنى.]»: الحسنى may be his good deeds, and it is their reward; or الحسنى may be Paradise, and you put الجزاء in construct with it though it is the same thing, as He said ﴿حَقُّ اليَقِين﴾ (the truth of certainty), ﴿دِينُ القَيِّمةِ﴾ (the religion of the upright), and ﴿ولَدَارُ الآخِرَةِ خَيْرٌ﴾ (and the home of the Hereafter is better). Had you made (الحسنى) nominative, having made الجزاء nominative and nunated it, that would be a valid aspect, but no one has read it so. It would then be like the reading of Masrūq: ﴿إِنَّا زَيَّنا السَّمَاءَ الدُّنْيَا بِزِينَةٍ الكَوَاكِب﴾ (indeed We adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment — the stars), giving الكواكب the genitive as an explication (tarjama) of "the adornment".

farraa:90-90.t: His saying: ﴿لَّمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُمْ مِّن دُونِهَا سِتْراً﴾ (for whom We had not made against it any shield): he says: no mountain, no cover and no tree; they are naked.

farraa:94-94.t: His saying: ﴿يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ﴾ (Gog and Magog): ʿĀṣim pronounced them with hamza, and no one else did. [His saying: ﴿فَهَلْ نَجْعَلُ لَكَ خَرْجاً﴾ (may we assign for you a tribute?)]: الخراج is the primary noun, and الخرج is like the maṣdar (verbal noun); it is like a fee (الجُعْل).

farraa:95-95.t: His saying: ﴿مَا مَكَّنِّي﴾ (that in which [my Lord] has established me): its nūn was assimilated into the nūn after it. It has been reported from Mujāhid (Abū Ṭalḥa al-Nāqiṭ mentioned it; I do not recall it from anyone else) that he read (مَا مَكَّنَنى) with two overt nūns, which is the original form.

farraa:96-96.t:
His saying: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا سَاوَىٰ بَيْنَ ٱلصَّدَفَيْنِ﴾ (until, when he had levelled [it] between the two mountain walls), and (الصُّدُفَيْنِ) and (الصُّدْفَيْنِ): ساوى and سوَّى بينهما are one (in meaning).
[His saying: ﴿آتُونِيۤ أُفْرِغْ عَلَيْهِ﴾ (bring me, that I may pour over it)]: Ḥamza and al-Aʿmash read (قال أْتُونِى) (short), making القطر (molten copper) accusative by it, and they took it (as from جيئونى, "come to me"); and (آتُونى) is "give me". When you lengthen the alif, it is good: ﴿آتِنَا غَدَاءَنَا﴾ (bring us our morning meal); "give me molten copper that I may pour it over it". When you do not lengthen the alif, you put the bāʾ «[Translator's note: the text has "الياء"; the example shows the preposition bāʾ is meant.]» on the accusative object and say: ائِتنا بغدائِنا (bring us our meal). The reading of Ḥamza and al-Aʿmash is correct and permissible in two ways. It may be like your saying: أخذت الخِطَام and أخذت بالخطام (I took the halter); or it may be on the basis of dropping the first hamza in (آتونى): when you drop the first, you pronounce the second with hamza.

farraa:98-98.t: His saying: ﴿جَعَلَهُ دَكَّآءَ﴾ (He will make it level): Abū al-ʿAbbās told us: Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ told me, from Saʿīd ibn Masrūq, from al-Shaʿbī, from al-Rabīʿ ibn Khaytham al-Thawrī, that a man recited to him (دكّاً), and he said: (دَكَّاءَ) — "make it full" (فخِّمها). Al-Farrāʾ said: he means: lengthen it.

farraa:100-100.t: His saying: ﴿وَعَرَضْنَا جَهَنَّمَ يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ (and We will present Hell that day): We will bring it out so that the disbelievers look at it. And أعرضت هى (it presented itself): it became clear and manifest.

farraa:101-101.t: His saying: ﴿لاَ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَمْعاً﴾ (they were not able to hear): as you say: they are not able to hear guidance and so be guided.

farraa:102-102.t: His saying: ﴿أَفَحَسِبَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوۤاْ﴾ (then do those who disbelieve think): the reading of the companions of ʿAbdallāh and of Mujāhid is (أَفَحَسِبَ). Abū al-ʿAbbās told us: Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Muḥammad ibn al-Mufaḍḍal al-Khurāsānī told me, from al-Ṣalt ibn Bihrām, from a man whom he named, from ʿAlī, that he read (أفحَسْبَ الذِينَ كَفَروا) (is it then sufficient for those who disbelieve). If you say (أَفَحَسْبُ الذين كَفرُوا), then أن is nominative; and if you say (أفحَسِبَ), أن is accusative.

farraa:108-108.t: His saying: ﴿عَنْهَا حِوَلاً﴾ (any transfer from it): a moving away.
